manifest.name: whalesong-studio
manifest.description: Whalesong Studio (鲸歌工坊), a long-form fiction studio for DeepSeek Harness: a showrunner agent and a crew of role agents (continuity, planning, directing, post-production) on the Harness's own agent loop, a dedicated prose model, a story bible, ensemble cast tracking, illustrations, audio drama, motion comics, videos and playable interludes
manifest.author: Dr. Xu

scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run test && node scripts/build.mjs --stage
scripts.release: npm run typecheck && npm run test && node scripts/build.mjs

bundle.text:
# whalesong-studio bundle patch.
#
# Applied after the Harness base and Web layers. It inserts two rows:
#
#   novel-writer      the Host half: project store, model routing, pipelines,
#                     jobs, and the routes Whalesong Studio talks to. Because this
#                     package declares `dsh.client`, the same row also puts the
#                     Studio (lib/client.js) on the browser roster.
#
#   preset-novelist   an agent preset. Sessions that select it get the
#                     showrunner persona and the novel_* tools; other sessions
#                     are untouched. The crew's roles run as children of such a
#                     session and join this same composition: what is mounted
#                     here is what a role can be given (Whalesong Studio → Settings →
#                     Crew decides how much of it each role sees).
#
# What it depends on, beyond what every DSH has: the subagent service
# (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent`, row `subagent` of the base bundle, on by
# default). Every role of the crew is a subagent of the conversation it works
# for; with that row switched off the roles fall back to one request, one
# answer — and the Studio says so at its top rather than doing it quietly.
#
# A profile's own cordis.patch.yml can override either row by id. A patch
# replaces a row's whole `config`, so restate every key you keep.

- insert:
    - id: novel-writer
      name: whalesong-studio
      config:
        # Deployment defaults for the Studio's settings (models, context,
        # image / tts / embedding endpoints). What a user saves in the Studio
        # overlays them. See docs/configuration.md.
        settings: {}

    - id: preset-novelist
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: novelist
        name: 小说家 Novelist
        description: 鲸歌工坊的总编：统筹设定、大纲、写作、修订与演出，正文交给写手模型。Whalesong Studio's showrunner for long-form fiction.
        order: 5
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                You are the showrunner of a fiction studio — an editor-in-chief
                who helps one author plan, write and stage a long novel. You are
                powered by the {{model}} model.
              # No `suffix: Your working directory is {{cwd}}.`: DSH 0.2.1 has no `{{cwd}}` and fails a prompt that
              # names it. The agent half says where the session works on a DSH that needs telling (src/agent/mount.ts).

          # Tools, showrunner instructions, project digest, /novel command.
          - id: novel-agent
            name: whalesong-studio/agent

          # Project and user instructions (AGENTS.md) still apply to a writing session.
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536

          # Files of the workspace: reference material, scripts, what the crew
          # produces. The manuscript itself is changed through the novel_* tools.
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false

          # Research.
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000

          # A shell and its background jobs, for work around the book. The crew's
          # post-production cuts video with it (ffmpeg); a book's own files stay
          # behind the novel_* tools whoever holds the shell.
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'

          # Outside help: DSH's own delegation tool, pointed at the Claude Code and
          # Codex subagent providers. Each tool appears only once its provider is
          # installed in the profile (@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code,
          # @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex); without them these rows do nothing.
          - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
            config:
              provider: claude-code
              toolName: subagent_claude_code
              backgroundMode: one-shot
              enableRunInBackground: false
              maxDepth: provider-managed
          - id: tool-subagent-codex
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
            config:
              provider: codex
              toolName: subagent_codex
              backgroundMode: one-shot
              enableRunInBackground: false
              maxDepth: provider-managed

          # Asking the author, tracking work, long-running objectives.
          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: false
          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'

          # Workflow guides shipped with this package, next to the author's own skills.
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
            config:
              customSkillDirs:
                - !!js process.getBuiltinModule('node:path').join(process.getBuiltinModule('node:path').dirname(process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(baseUrl).resolve('whalesong-studio/package.json')), 'skills')
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

          # Long sessions: compact history, prune oversized tool results.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 12000
                  headChars: 6000
                  tailChars: 2000

readme.text: English · 简体中文 · Tutorial · Everything it does · Website
**Write a long novel with a crew of AI agents — a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).**

**Whalesong Studio** (鲸歌工坊) is for writing long fiction with AI. You talk to a showrunner; behind it, a small crew writes, keeps track of the story, reviews, draws and gives it a voice. Hundreds of thousands of words in, your characters are still themselves and the story still adds up. When the book is done, you can publish it as an illustrated website in one click.

It isn't a role-play front end or a "generate a chapter" button: you make the calls, and each model does the part it is good at.
<sub>*Lewis Carroll's* Alice's Adventures in Wonderland *imported into the Studio, open beside a conversation with the showrunner. Every picture in these screenshots was drawn in the Studio.*</sub>

**See what it makes:** two classics published with Whalesong Studio — read *[Alice's Adventures in Wonderland](https://whalesong.xuhao1.me/books/alice/)* or *[Dream of the Red Chamber](https://whalesong.xuhao1.me/books/hongloumeng/)* (红楼梦, in Chinese) online. The first chapters can be listened to as well — the first three of *Alice*, the first ten of 红楼梦 — voiced by the Studio. Once inside, click **People** and **World** at the top: every character has a page of their own, the main ones with portraits, and the places can be walked into one inside another.
> **New here?** The [tutorial](./docs/tutorial.md) walks you through it with screenshots, from installing to your first illustrated chapter.

readme.section: A crew, not a single model
readme.text: Models that plan well and use tools well rarely write beautiful prose, and the best prose writers rarely manage a big project well. So Whalesong Studio doesn't ask one model to do everything:

readme.section: A crew, not a single model
readme.text:
| Role | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Showrunner** (总编) | The one you talk to, on any model you like. Works out what you want, plans what comes next, hands out the work and reports back. It never writes the story itself. |
| **Writer** (写手) | Writes the prose, on a model you choose. Before every chapter it is handed everything that chapter needs: the setting, where each character stands, what came before, the open threads, the outline and the style. |
| **Continuity** (场记) | Remembers. After every chapter it notes what happened and how everyone has changed. It also reviews like an editor — and when it says something contradicts an earlier chapter, it shows you the passage. |
| **Planner** (策划) | Has the ideas. Works out what could happen next, fleshes out the characters and the world, tries "what if…" turns of the story, and can look things up on the web. |
| **Director** (导演) | Sound and pictures. Adapts chapters into audio drama and storyboards, and plays everyone else when you step into a scene as one of the characters. |
| **Post-production** (后期) | Edits voices, sound and pictures into a video, checks the result itself, and hands it over only when it passes. |

readme.section: A crew, not a single model
readme.text: The four crew members are real agents running on DeepSeek Harness's own agent loop, and every job they do leaves a full record in your conversation: what they looked up, what they handed in, what it cost. Prefer buttons to chat? Everything can be done from the Studio's own screens, too.

readme.section: Hundreds of thousands of words in, nothing is forgotten
readme.text: After every chapter the Studio notes what happened, where each character stands and which threads moved. When the next chapter is written, the writer gets a summary of everything before plus the last few chapters in full — the whole book, while it's short enough — along with any earlier passages that matter. A style profile keeps the voice steady. Ask for what comes next, a fix to a paragraph, a rewrite of a chapter or one change carried through the whole book: every change is shown to you first, side by side, and the previous version is always kept.

readme.section: Every character gets a page, every place can be explored
readme.text: Each character has a card — personality, relationships, what they go through in the book, how they look and sound — and every later picture and spoken line follows it. Places nest inside one another: Wonderland holds the hall of doors, the wood, the garden and the March Hare's house. Beside the text, **People** shows each character's page with a large portrait, and **World** opens any place to show its picture, what it contains and who lives there.

readme.section: Every character gets a page, every place can be explored
readme.text:
| | |
|---|---|
|  |  |
| *People — who they are, how they look, what they go through* | *World — what is in a place, and who lives there* |

readme.section: Read it, hear it, watch it
readme.text: A reader with careful typography and the book's own pictures in the text; one switch turns it into an audiobook, with every character keeping one voice through the whole book. Pictures stay consistent too: each character first gets a design sheet — front, side and back — and every later picture is drawn to match. Go further with an **audio drama**, a **motion comic** that plays along with the voices, a chapter cut into a **video**, or an **interlude** — play one of the characters in a scene while the others answer you.

readme.section: Read it, hear it, watch it
readme.text:
| | |
|---|---|
|  |  |
| *Read — and with one switch, listen* | *Gallery — one look per book; every picture remembers how it was made* |

The pictures can come from any image model you like — GPT Image, Qwen-Image, FLUX, Seedream… or a model running on your own computer.

readme.section: Publish it as a work of digital art
readme.text: When the book is ready, publish it as a website in one click: the text set for reading, a portrait and a short biography for every character, and places your readers can step into. Nothing to install, and it reads well on a phone. The two classics linked above were made exactly this way.

readme.section: Bring in a book you've already written
readme.text: Drop in a `.txt`, `.md`, `.epub` or `.docx`. The Studio finds the chapters, sorts out the characters and the world, rebuilds the outline and learns the style — then you can carry on writing, revise it, or turn it into an audio drama. The screenshots on this page are *Alice's Adventures in Wonderland* imported this way; the Chinese README shows *Dream of the Red Chamber*.

- **Your book is an ordinary folder** of Markdown and JSON. Edit it in the Studio, in your own editor or through the showrunner — all three see the same files, and it works well with git.
- **Branching plots**: try another way the story could go on a branch; whichever works better becomes the main line, and nothing you wrote is lost.
- **On your phone** over Wi-Fi with one button, read-only or editable.
- **Private books**: lock a book — text, pictures, audio and your conversations about it — behind a password or your computer's own unlock.
- **Export** to Markdown, plain text, HTML or EPUB, and see **usage and cost** per model, book and day.
Everything it does, in full: **[docs/features.md](./docs/features.md)**.
Requires DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` or later (`< 0.3`). It works in the Desktop app and the Web UI (`dsh web`).
The Desktop app owns its `desktop` profile, so plugins are installed from inside the app — `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` is refused by design.
To upgrade, uninstall the plugin on the same page and add the new version. Your books are ordinary directories in your workspaces and are not touched.

`dsh plugin` runs pnpm, which must be on your `PATH`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/whalesong-studio-0.1.0.tgz
dsh plugin --profile web remove whalesong-studio
```

A built checkout path or `github:xuhao1/whalesong-studio` works in place of the tarball; for the latter pnpm must be allowed to run the build script, see [Package and install a plugin](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/develop/basic/publish).

Needs Node.js 22+.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/xuhao1/whalesong-studio.git
cd whalesong-studio
npm install     # installs dependencies; builds lib/ when the checkout has none
npm pack        # writes whalesong-studio-<version>.tgz
The [tutorial](./docs/tutorial.md) does the same step by step, with screenshots; this is the short version.

1. Open **Whalesong Studio** in the left sidebar. The first time, it asks you to **connect the models**: pick a service, paste one API key and click **Set up** — pictures, voices and search are configured at once. Writing uses the text models you already have in DeepSeek Harness, so you can also skip this and come back later. **With ChatGPT Plus or Pro**, press **Sign in with ChatGPT and set up** on the first card and sign in once in the browser: writing and pictures are both connected, no key ([step by step](./docs/chatgpt.md)).
2. **Start a new book** from a sentence or a paragraph about the story. Tick "draft the foundation" and the planner proposes a premise, the main characters, the world, volumes and the opening chapters — all yours to change. Or **bring in a book you've written** by dropping in the file.
3. Start a session with the **小说家 Novelist** preset and say what you want: "write chapter two and end it on the knock at the door", "the villain feels flat — give him a reason", "what if she turns the deal down?", "make chapter one into an audio drama". The Studio opens beside the conversation as soon as the work starts.
4. Read the chapter in the Studio and select anything
In the message box, `/novel status`, `/novel mode <ideate|bible|outline|draft|revise|review|stage|play>`, `/novel digest` and `/novel export <format>` work as well.

Everything lives in *Whalesong Studio → Settings*, and the showrunner will change any of it for you if you ask. **Writing uses DeepSeek Harness's own models** — whatever you've connected under its *Settings → Models*; in the Studio you just choose which role uses which. **A ChatGPT subscription** is the exception: DSH can sign in to ChatGPT by itself but has no page that starts it — the ChatGPT card on the Studio's guide page does, and one sign-in adds the route to DSH and gives the roles GPT models ([On ChatGPT Plus / Pro](./docs/chatgpt.md)). The Studio itself only needs models for pictures, voices and search, and one key sets them all up:

| Service | Images | Speech | Retrieval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aliyun Bailian | Qwen-Image 3.0 | qwen-audio-3.1-tts-next | qwen3.7-text-embedding-flash |
| OpenRouter | **GPT Image 2.5** | Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS | Qwen3 Embedding 8B |
| OpenAI | GPT Image 2 | gpt-4o-mini-tts | text-embedding-3-small |
| ChatGPT subscription (Plus / Pro) | the subscription's GPT Image; writing too. One sign-in, no key | — | — |

Or set each one up yourself: any OpenAI-compatible service, ComfyUI, or a model on your own computer. Keys are kept in DeepSeek Harness's credential store, never in a settings file. Every option in detail: [docs/configuration.md](./docs/configuration.md).

| | |
|---|---|
| [Tutorial](./docs/tutorial.md) | from installing to the album, with screenshots |
| [On ChatGPT Plus / Pro](./docs/chatgpt.md) | one sign-in, and writing and pictures run on the subscription |
| [Everything it does](./docs/features.md) | every part of the Studio, in full |
| [Configuration](./docs/configuration.md) | each setting, per-book overrides, deployment defaults |
| [What a book looks like on disk](./docs/project-format.md) | the files of a book, field by field |
| [Design and internals](./docs/design.md) | why the roles are split, the memory layers, the context packer, the stage pipelines ([中文](./docs/design.zh.md)) |
| [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) | the layout of the code, the dev server, the tests |
| [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md) | what changed in each release |

- Text goes to the models you chose for the roles: a role that follows the conversation model or uses a Harness model goes through the Harness LLM runtime (the same routes, credentials and retry policy as your conversations); a role with an endpoint of its own is called by the Studio directly.
- Image prompts, the text of lines to be spoken and (if enabled) text chunks to be embedded go to the media endpoints you configured. Nothing is sent to any endpoint you did not configure; there is no telemetry.
- Keys stay in the Harness credential store on your machine and are only ever sent to the endpoint host they were entered for.
- Books stay in your workspace. Settings live in `$DSH_HOME/novel-writer/`.
